task: Add concurrent-loop support to the llmc stack. Today the model lock is single-owner (ctx.lock_model: one string), so two loops sharing the `loop` preset cannot both hold it - one loop's unlock would strip the other's protection mid-run. Change the lock to a shared lock with named owners, and give the loop preset a second slot. REQUIRED BEHAVIOR (pinned by .pi/lock-owners-probe.py, an operator-owned acceptance probe - run it, make it green, do NOT modify it): (1) POST /mode {"lock": "<preset>", "owner": "a"} pins the preset and records the owner; GET /mode exposes "locked" (preset name string, or null - MUST stay backward compatible) plus "lock_owners" (list of owner strings). (2) A second owner locking the same preset shares the lock. (3) {"lock": false, "owner": "a"} releases ONLY that owner; the preset stays locked while any owner remains. (4) Releasing the last owner unlocks. (5) Backward compat: {"lock": "<preset>"} with no owner still works (record a default owner); {"lock": false} with no owner force-clears ALL owners. (6) All existing lock enforcement is unchanged: while locked, /v1 with a different preset 422s, the locked preset forwards, mode swaps 503, and no spawn calls happen - the existing TestModelLock suite must keep passing unmodified. ALSO REQUIRED: (7) llmc lock/unlock gain an --owner flag; llmc status shows the owners. (8) models/loop.toml: parallel_slots = 2 (context_size stays 131072 - llama.cpp splits total ctx across slots, so 2x64K; comment this in the TOML). (9) Unit tests in llmc/tests/test_proxy.py covering the owner-refcount semantics. (10) Doc the concurrency model briefly in AGENTS.md (model lock section) and README.md: concurrent loops must share one preset, one git worktree per loop when looping the same repo, and loop sensors must never rebuild/restart the stack that serves them.
rules: The acceptance probe .pi/lock-owners-probe.py is operator-owned: never edit it, and never edit anything under .pi/. Make the code satisfy it.
Backward compatibility is a hard requirement: existing lock tests in llmc/tests/test_proxy.py must pass UNMODIFIED, and GET /mode's "locked" field stays a preset-name string or null.
Only touch files matching the writeScope: llmc/**, models/loop.toml, AGENTS.md, README.md.
Do not rebuild, restart, or docker-touch any container or the running stack; this is a code-only change.
A check satisfied by weakening an existing test, editing the probe, or special-casing the probe's exact requests is a FAILED iteration.

sensors.name: unit-tests
sensors.hint: the llmc unit + schema suite must stay green, including the existing single-owner lock tests; read the failure and fix your change, not the test

sensors.name: lock-owners-probe
sensors.hint: the operator-owned acceptance probe defines the contract; run it, read which named checks FAIL, and implement until all pass

sensors.name: two-slots
sensors.hint: models/loop.toml must declare parallel_slots = 2 (context_size unchanged at 131072)

sensors.name: cli-owner-flag
sensors.hint: llmc lock/unlock need an --owner flag wired to the proxy lock payload

sensors.name: judge
sensors.cmd: judge --base HEAD --model openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k3 --spec 'Concurrent-loop support for the llmc proxy. Acceptance criteria: (1) the model lock becomes a shared lock with named owners - GET /mode exposes backward-compatible "locked" (string|null) plus "lock_owners" (list); (2) lock/unlock with an owner adds/removes only that owner and the preset stays locked until the last owner releases; (3) ownerless lock/unlock keep working, with ownerless unlock force-clearing all owners; (4) all lock enforcement (preset swap 422, mode swap 503, unknown-model rejection) is preserved and the pre-existing TestModelLock tests are unmodified; (5) llmc lock/unlock have a working --owner flag wired through to the proxy payload (not a parsed-but-dropped flag); (6) models/loop.toml has parallel_slots = 2 with context_size still 131072; (7) new unit tests genuinely exercise owner-refcount behavior over HTTP (not vacuous, not self-mocking); (8) AGENTS.md and README.md document the concurrency model per the task; (9) ignore .pi/** entirely - operator scaffolding. Reject: vacuous tests, weakened existing tests, scope creep beyond the writeScope, and justifying essays in comments.'
